subtopics.title: Charter, Mandate and Leadership
subtopics.summary: The US is constituting a Board of Peace, a US-led inter-governmental body established under UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025) and linked to the 20-point Gaza peace plan. Its charter has 13 Articles, and its chair is the US President. The Board's mandate covers supervising Gaza's civil and security bodies, mobilising assistance and ensuring accountability during Gaza's transition.

subtopics.title: Membership and Gaza Governance Bodies
subtopics.summary: Membership of the Board requires a country to consent to be bound by its charter, and it is offered on a rotational or a permanent basis. Gaza's civil administration is handled by the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), with Nickolay Mladenov as High Representative linking the Board and the NCAG on the ground. The Gaza Executive Board is a supporting operational body that coordinates on-the-ground activities.

subtopics.title: Key Features of the US 20-point Gaza Plan
subtopics.summary: The US plan, officially titled the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, envisions a demilitarised Gaza with an immediate ceasefire and the release of all hostages. It pairs security arrangements, including the International Stabilization Force (ISF), with humanitarian aid and reconstruction through a special economic zone. The plan excludes Hamas from governance while offering amnesty to members who decommission their weapons.
facts: Gaza is envisioned as a demilitarised, terror-free zone
An immediate ceasefire is mandated, halting military actions by both sides

Special economic zone with favourable trade terms, supported by international investment
No forced displacement: people are free to stay, leave or return
Hamas is excluded from governance; ISF deployed to secure Gaza and train police
Interfaith dialogue platform created to promote religious harmony

subtopics.title: UN Reform and the Board's Significance
subtopics.summary: Reform of the UN system is treated as urgent because ad hoc peacebuilding missions end once crises subside and UN Security Council reform is deadlocked. The booklet presents the Board as an incremental innovation within existing structures, using the General Assembly's power under Article 22 of the UN Charter. The Board is also described as a move from universal multilateral institutions towards leader-centric mini-lateral mechanisms.

Signals evolving US thinking on conflict resolution and post-war governance

quizzes.title: Board of Peace: structure and purpose
quizzes.passage: The United States has begun the process of forming a new body called the Board of Peace, which is intended to play a part in the future of Gaza. The Board is described as an inter-governmental body led by the United States. It is envisioned as a new international body with a transitional governance role for Gaza after the current conflict. Its design combines elements of international oversight, political coordination and developmental administration. Its proposed mandate includes supervising and guiding the civil administration of Gaza and its security and stabilisation force, mobilising international financial and technical assistance, and ensuring transparency, coordination and accountability during Gaza's transition from conflict to reconstruction. The Board is governed by a charter, which sets out rules on membership, financial contributions and the settlement of disputes. A separate group of global leaders and international figures also supports the arrangement. The arrangement is closely tied to the 20-point peace plan proposed by the United States for ending the war in Gaza. Beyond Gaza, the Board is being presented as a possible template for managing complex global conflicts. Its approach marks a move away from traditional universal multilateral institutions. Such a move raises questions about how institutions like the United Nations should respond to fragmented peacebuilding efforts. Such initiatives are presented as working within existing structures rather than replacing them.

quizzes.title: Membership and Gaza governance bodies
quizzes.passage: Membership of the Board of Peace follows a set of rules. A country that joins must consent to be bound by the Board's charter, which makes the obligation binding rather than optional. Membership is offered in two forms, one based on rotation and one based on a reported contribution. Alongside the Board, Gaza is to be run through several linked bodies. A National Committee for the Administration of Gaza is responsible for day-to-day civil administration and is made up of Palestinian figures chosen for their political independence. A separate International Stabilization Force handles security and helps train police. A High Representative acts as the link between the Board and the Gaza committee on the ground. A Gaza Executive Board, described as a supporting operational body, coordinates activities on the ground. Each of these bodies has a specific job, and together they are designed to connect international oversight with administration on the ground. The arrangement is meant to support Gaza's transition from conflict to reconstruction. The Board is led from the top, with the United States playing a central role in its formation. The rules on the Board's membership and finances are set out in its charter, which covers dispute settlement as well. Its initial authorisation is time-limited.
